candidate_sources.README.md:
# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

checkpoints: A warm source delivers its cached initial frame to the panel; later packets continue to stream.
Immediate and deferred decoding both retain one progress-history effect per admitted completion.
Publish a newer-received frame, then finish an older decode: retain both history effects without replacing the newer display.
A later-received frame with a lower progress value can display; freshness is not numeric monotonicity.
Check freshness across attempts belonging to the same visit.
Navigate or deliver another frame from recordProgress and showProgress callbacks; verify current visit authority and display ordering.
During synchronous startup, hide, switch, or reopen the same file, then emit another packet before startup returns; verify retired reception, retained accepted history, and newer ownership.
Navigate from listener removal and cancellation callbacks; verify that older operations do not overwrite newer ownership.
Retry while cancellation navigates: retain exactly one entry-bound retry record and transfer, cancel the retired result, and suppress its queued notice.
Verify repeated cleanup, disposal, independent workspaces, same-file reuse, unchanged queue and notice shapes, and unchanged telemetry bootstrap and live-delta behavior.
forbidden_effects: Losing the cached initial panel update or ordinary subsequent progress.
Allowing an older-received frame to replace a newer frame already published in the current visit.
Suppressing a required progress-history effect solely because its visit retired or its display result is stale.
Painting or publishing a queued notice for a retired visit, including after the identical file is selected again.
Allowing additional packets from a retired startup subscription to initiate new decoding.
Letting an older operation overwrite ownership established by synchronous newer navigation.
Changing diagnostic telemetry to count cached bootstrap data.
Adding byteCount or otherwise changing queue-record fields without separate authorization.
lifecycle_identity: A selection creates a distinct visit, including selection of the same file again; retry retains the visit and creates a new attempt.
The feed can be shared by multiple attempts and visits; feed or file identity alone does not establish panel authority.
Progress history remains associated with the file and attempt that admitted the packet.
Visible progress belongs to the current visit. Display freshness must span attempts within that visit because they paint the same panel.
Each workspace owns its visit counter, attempt counter, task collection, and disposal state.

obligations.text: Install panel progress reception before invoking callback-capable source startup so synchronous cached packets produce the initial update, while preserving later streaming and feed reuse.

Distinguish reception eligibility, retained history, and presentation authority. Once a packet is admitted, preserve its existing record-before-receive completion behavior. Retirement stops further admission and visible output, but does not erase history work already admitted.

Track frame age by packet reception order for the display-owning visit. Once a newer frame has been published, suppress older completions from presentation while retaining their history effects. Recheck authority and freshness after recordProgress callbacks and commit publication ordering before invoking showProgress.

Preserve navigation and cleanup ownership across synchronous startup, listener removal, cancellation, and host callbacks. Retirement must take effect during startup even before a returned cleanup handle becomes available. Reconcile and release retired resources without replacing resources owned by newer navigation.

Preserve accepted retry behavior: capture the entry visit and file, cancel the previous attempt before enqueueing, create and record exactly one accepted retry even if cancellation navigates, cancel its resulting handle if its visit ended, and publish its queued notice only while that visit remains current.

Preserve public transfer and adapter behavior, queue-record and notice payloads, record-before-transfer ordering, idempotent cancellation and disposal, independent workspace state, ordinary streaming, and subsequent uses.
Keep diagnostic telemetry behavior unchanged, including starting before listening so its own cached bootstrap is excluded and retaining its existing handling of live decoded deltas.

ordering_barriers: Panel listener registration must precede feed.start(). Telemetry retains its existing distinct ordering.
Determine reception identity and frame order before decode or other callback-capable packet processing.
Preserve record(frame) before receive(frame); presentation checks must occur after the history callback returns.
Commit a frame's publication ordering before calling showProgress, which can synchronously reenter delivery or navigation.
Retire current ownership before releasing the previous visit; recheck navigation authority after release callbacks return.
Preserve cancellation order: abort the signal, stop progress reception, then invoke onCancel.
Preserve retry cancellation before enqueueing and queue recording before transfer construction.
preservation: Queue records remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}; notices remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}.
Queue records remain retained after their originating visit ends.
Accepted decoded progress records history before attempting current-visit presentation.
Cancellation is idempotent; disposal is idempotent and cancels retained tasks.
Listener removal commits before the synchronous host detach callback; repeated removal is inert.
Selection and hiding clear current ownership before releasing old resources; nested newer navigation retains ownership.
A retry remains bound to its captured visit even if cancel callbacks navigate.
Already admitted decoding from a canceled attempt can still paint if its visit remains current and its frame is sufficiently fresh.
scope: Draft contract only; no workspace modifications.
Repair panel progress reception and necessary lifecycle and display-order coordination using TASK and supplied public documents/code as normative evidence.
Preserve tests, configuration, public interfaces, and diagnostic consumer behavior.

current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.
